- When sentiment is negative (e.g., -0.25 or 0.50), model tends to overcorrect downward; adjust forecast downward by 1–2% of recent range.
- Model consistently overestimates prices in early 30-day forecasts, especially after recent spikes; apply 1–3% downward bias to first 5–7 days.
- After a sharp price spike, model often overshoots in the following 5–10 days; reduce forecast by 2–5% for next 3–5 days.
- If sentiment is neutral or positive, model tends to overreact to short-term volatility; apply smoothing filter (e.g., 3-day moving average) to reduce noise.
- Mean reversion is strong in 10–15 day horizons; if forecast deviates >3% from 10-day moving average, adjust toward it.
- In low-sentiment periods, model underestimates downside risk; add 0.5–1.5% buffer for potential drop in next 3–5 days.
- Forecast horizon >15 days shows increasing lag; reduce forecast by 0.5–1.5% per 5-day lag to account for delayed market reaction.
